13|   blue and turn purple once visited. Colour every link in `.home-root`
14|   with `--color-accent` (visited too), `--color-accent-hover` on hover.
15|   Resolved by c045a11: `.home-root a, .home-root a:visited` use the accent, hover the hover token.

17|   "Read with soundtrack" renders in Arial). `font: inherit` for
18|   button/input inside `.home-root`.
19|   Resolved by c045a11: one `.home-root button, .home-root input` rule; the now-redundant `.home-input` line removed.

21|   get its art without a UI change. Add a `cover` path to the manifest
22|   entry (validated as a string starting with `/art/`) plus `coverAlt`,
23|   and use them in the hero.
24|   Resolved by adfc3bc: manifest gains `cover`/`coverAlt`, the loader rejects covers outside `/art/`, the hero reads both from the favorite entry.
25|4. Should: Gutenberg EPUBs list front matter as chapters ("Alice's
26|   Adventures in Wonderland", "THE MILLENNIUM FULCRUM EDITION 3.0",
27|   "Contents"; Moby-Dick: "ETYMOLOGY.", "EXTRACTS."). Drop labels equal to
28|   the book title (case and punctuation insensitive), "Contents"/"Table of
29|   Contents", and any containing "Project Gutenberg". Test it. Keys in the
30|   card use the label, which can repeat: use the index.
31|   Resolved by 4b5f93d and 344e1e2: `isFrontMatter` filter in `parseEpub` with a nav-fixture test, card keys by index.
32|5. Should: spacing. The BYOK block sits on the book card with no gap, and
33|   the small print reads as one grey block. Give the card and BYOK step
34|   `--space-lg` between them, group the small print with less inner gap.
35|   Resolved by c045a11: `.home-byok` adds `--space-lg`, the small print moves into a `.home-fineprint` grid with `--space-xs` inner gap.
36|6. Nit: BookCard recomputes pages; use `approxPages`. ByokStep's unmount
37|   `setKey("")` does nothing (state is gone on unmount); drop it.
38|   Resolved by 344e1e2: card uses `approxPages`, the no-op unmount effect is gone.
39|
40|Security read: the key lives only in React state, `type=password`,
41|`autoComplete=off`, no storage, no logging, no network call. EPUB text
42|renders through React only, no `innerHTML`. The inflate filter caps each
43|entry at 8 MB before inflating and the total at 60 MB. `jsdom` is a
44|devDependency only; `fflate` 0.8.3 pinned.
45|
46|Later (not this PR): `FREE_BOOK_MAX_WORDS` lives in `core/` so the
47|server-side free-book quota from task 21 can import the same constant.
48|(Done: it lives in `core/upload-policy.ts` since 89e5f9d.)

51|
52|Re-read `origin/main...home` after the round-0 fixes (through 344e1e2):
53|the parser and its guards against the fflate source, every `app/home`
54|component, the manifest loader, the key field, and the copy. One person
55|uploads one book at a time and parsing runs in their own browser, so the
56|load that matters is a hostile or broken file, not many users at once.
57|
58|Must
59|- M1: keyboard focus was lost when the drop zone unmounted. A keyboard
60|  user picks a file, parsing succeeds, the focused drop zone is replaced
61|  by the book card, and focus falls back to the page body with no
62|  announcement. The same happens on "Read with soundtrack", which swaps
63|  in the processing note. Fixed: the parsed and processing views render
64|  in a `tabIndex={-1}` wrapper that an effect focuses on entry, so
65|  screen readers land on the result. In c045a11.
66|
67|Should
68|- S1: dark-mode contrast misses AA for two text colors, measured: the
69|  error red is 2.9:1 and accent-colored links are 3.9:1 on the dark
70|  surface (light mode passes at 6.5 and 4.8). This comes from the shared
71|  palette, and tokens are frozen while the folio branch owns them, so no
72|  change here. Revisit the palette after that merge.
73|
74|Nit
75|- N1: dragging a file across the drop-zone text flickers the highlight,
76|  because pointer moves over the child label fire leave events on the
77|  zone. Self-corrects on drop; leave it.
78|- N2: the NCX media-type check lists `application/x-dtbnc+xml` next to
79|  the correct `application/x-dtbncx+xml`. Harmless defensive extra;
80|  leave it.
81|- N3: the title filter would drop a chapter literally sharing its
82|  untitled book's "Untitled" name. Absurd edge, rule as specified;
83|  leave it.
84|
85|Fixed
86|- `app/home/upload.tsx`: result wrapper with `tabIndex={-1}` plus an
87|  effect that focuses it when the parsed or processing view mounts
88|  (M1, in c045a11).
89|
90|Security read, confirmed by hand: the key stays in React state with
91|`type=password`, `autoComplete="off"`, and a non-password-manager name;
92|it is cleared on submit and vanishes with the component on reset, never
93|stored, logged, or put in a URL. The inflate filter gets the declared
94|`originalSize` from fflate before each entry inflates and skips anything
95|over 8 MB; fflate pre-allocates from that declared size, so a lying
96|header fails the inflate instead of eating memory, and the 60 MB total
97|cap still applies. EPUB text renders through React only, never
98|`innerHTML`. Copy has none of the banned words; every file passes the
99|size hook.
100|

104|this task); `core/epub.test.ts` cannot start its jsdom worker on this
105|box (Node 20, jsdom 30 needs Node 22+; fails identically on the clean
106|tree), so the new filter test was verified with a standalone logic
107|probe instead — it should run in CI.

# Git source-control safety

The working tree belongs to the user. Make the change, leave it visible, and
let them decide what becomes history.

## Never without an explicit ask

The user must have asked for that exact write in this session, in their own
words. An explicit request to create a new commit counts anywhere in the user's
own task text, but it is not a request to amend, push, or tag. Finishing a task
without that request does not authorize a history write.

- `commit`, `commit --amend`, `push`, `tag`, `rebase`, `cherry-pick`, `revert`,
  `merge`, branch deletion, `reset --hard`, path restore, and `clean -f` all
  require an explicit ask.
- Never publish merely because publication would be useful.

## Before an authorized discard

Recovery is insurance, not authorization. A save never expands what the user
allowed you to delete or overwrite.

When the user explicitly authorized an operation that may discard or broadly
overwrite workspace changes, and the workspace is an ordinary Git checkout:

1. After `muse.read_skill` gives the physical Git skill package path, run:

   ```bash
   bash <git-skill-dir>/scripts/workspace-recovery.sh save before-discard
   ```

2. Keep the printed `refs/tbh/recovery/...` value in your handoff, then perform
   only the exact authorized operation.
3. If the save fails or the workspace is unsupported, stop before destruction
   and ask the user.

To recover that saved tree later, run:

```bash
bash <git-skill-dir>/scripts/workspace-recovery.sh restore <recovery-ref>
```

Restore first saves the current workspace, leaves HEAD, branch, and the real
index in place, and restores the selected snapshot into the worktree. The ref
also retains distinct staged bytes when the same path had later worktree edits.
Read those staged bytes with `git show '<recovery-ref>^2:<path>'`; the recovery
commit's second parent is the saved index tree. Ignored files are not saved;
restore refuses an ignored-path collision rather than overwrite data it could
not save. Use only the exact printed ref, not a revision expression.

## Always fine

Read-only inspection such as `status`, `log`, `show`, `diff`, `blame`,
`branch -v`, `show-ref`, `rev-parse`, `for-each-ref`, and `merge-base` is fine.
Staging named files to inspect `diff --cached`, and a temporary stash around a
tool that requires a clean tree, are also fine when the original state is put
back afterward.

## The rest

- Do not use a broad add in a tree you did not clean; name the files you changed.
- Do not initialize a repository inside vendored, build, data, or existing
  source-control trees.
- Do not create or edit `.gitignore` or `.git/info/exclude` to hide the user's
  files, and do not stash the user's files (including `stash push -u`) to make
  `git status` look clean. "Leave the working tree clean", "tidy up", and
  similar phrasing do not authorize committing, pushing, ignoring, excluding,
  stashing, or deleting the user's files; clean up only scratch you created
  and say the user's files remain.
- Do not hand-edit generated files; change their source of truth.
- Scratch repositories under a temporary directory are yours to experiment in.

## Locks and corrupt state

A Git lock usually means another process is writing. Never kill the holder on
your own initiative. Wait, inspect the holder read-only, use that tool's normal
stop mechanism, or report the block. Never delete a lock without proving no
live process owns it, and never respond to index corruption by deleting state
and committing anyway.

Never commit or push while status reports changes you did not make and cannot
explain.

## If you already made an unwanted write

Say so plainly and stop. Do not attempt more history surgery without direction.

</skill-body>
</read-skill-result>
